implementedBehavior: Assistant is an optional module: importing, activating, and checking health with provider NONE does not initialize a provider or acquire model capabilities. External generation is disabled until the project feature-consent action explicitly enables it; credentials remain environment/host configuration.

Source-supported rewrite, setting QA, summaries, continuation, dialogue sketch, reader reaction, synonym, Zukan, state-event draft and deterministic aspect-review flows are exposed through snapshot-bound actions and the React contribution. Generated results retain model/provider/prompt identity and verified source citations where the source feature supplies them.

Rewrite choices remain unapproved until the author selects one and submits a separate Core proposal. Summary refresh and chapter/scene summary writes use source-freshness preconditions and one ordered proposal. Zukan proposals preserve validated manuscript or sandbox dialogue-sketch provenance and are created through Story. No Assistant handler writes canonical files, approves, checkpoints, publishes, or commits directly.

Source prompt previews return the actual source-context prompts locally. The continuation preview shares context assembly with generation, uses the selected scene/chapter/recent-sentence context and source token-budget calculation, and is classified as owner compute because it invokes bounded NLP and semantic actions.

Project model preferences are non-secret, versioned state submitted as a Core proposal. Imported historical usage JSONL bytes remain preserved under their existing owner; new provider-call usage goes to the host-owned durable usage store. New usage records preserve call identity/status/model/timing/cache metadata while omitting prompts, manuscript text and credentials.

The production owner API/runtime streamed real local Qwen rewrite deltas, cancelled after a received delta, durably retained the aborted call, streamed QA deltas and preserved a nonconforming citation result as a schema error, then returned three real rewrite alternatives. Repeated loopback runs exposed string citations and an unsupported citation kind; the assertion accepts only a nonempty array of recognized Zod issue objects with typed paths/messages or a recognized JSON syntax error, so arbitrary provider/network errors cannot satisfy it. No proposal or manuscript write occurred before choice. The author-selected candidate entered Core as a one-operation manuscript proposal with source revision reads; owner approval and checkpoint preceded publication. The test confirmed published bytes through a new CoreStore reconstruction and confirmed the host-owned usage event IDs survived that reload without retaining prompts or manuscript text. QA did not fabricate a schema-valid answer.

compositionLimits: This candidate evidence is scoped to Assistant unit/action tests, the Assistant browser contribution, one production owner-action preview, and one local-provider API/Core synthetic repository flow. The preview and browser tests do not substitute for the provider reference test.

The real QA stream produced a truthful schema error from the deliberately small local model. Source tool-loop and citation validation behavior is covered by the focused Assistant test; the provider acceptance allows only recognized JSON parse errors or structured Zod validation issues, and does not claim generative QA answer quality.

This artifact does not certify final full-profile browser/API composition, P12 legacy import/reactivation/reclone composition, final root acceptance, or OCI lifecycle. Those are recorded and gated by the campaign owners.
